item.title: US bans use of China’s DeepSeek AI tools by government agencies
item.description: <p>Use of tools ‘may result in the transfer of sensitive data’ to China, defense department says</p><p>The <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news">US</a> government on Monday ordered its agencies to stop using artificial intelligence (AI) tools from the Chinese startup <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/deepseek">DeepSeek</a>, as the countries race for dominance in the fast-moving sector.</p><p>A notice from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced the ban on products developed by DeepSeek – and tools created using DeepSeek by third parties – saying they must be removed from IT devices.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/20/us-bans-china-deepseek-ai-tools-government-agencies">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: The Guardian view on Trump and Putin: Ukraine’s future is not theirs to bargain away | Editorial
item.description: <p>Russia wants America and China to decide Ukraine’s future without Kyiv. Europe must challenge this dangerous return to diplomacy of the strong for the strong</p><p>Does Vladimir Putin know exactly how to play Donald&nbsp;Trump? The history of <a href="https://edition.cnn.com/2026/06/14/europe/trump-putin-phone-call-birthday">chummy</a> phone calls, high-profile <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Russia%E2%80%93United_States_summit">meetings</a> and attempts to bring Russia in from the cold certainly suggests that Moscow’s thuggish ruler has a hold on this American president. If Mr&nbsp;Trump agrees to <a href="https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/19/russia-explores-putin-trump-xi-summit-on-ukraine-deal">negotiate</a> Ukraine’s future with Mr&nbsp;Putin and China’s Xi Jinping without Ukraine at the&nbsp;table, he will have handed the Russian leader a victory before talks begin. The message will be that strongmen are ruling the world and determining the fate of weaker nations.</p><p>Ukraine has the right to determine its future. That right cannot be waved away by a self-serving Russian proposal, however much it indulges Mr Trump’s belief that world affairs should be settled by powerful men. The scales are <a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c64g18ljjd8do">falling</a> from European eyes. Trumpian America is raising doubts about whether it will help deter aggression or even honour its Nato commitments. If Washington now rewards Moscow and pressures Ukraine to accept a raw deal, it would be a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/volodymyr-zelenskyy-feels-betrayed-by-donald-trump-over-starlink-access">betrayal</a>. European governments would wonder where America might be in&nbsp;the future when their own security is threatened.</p><p><em><strong>Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/tone/letters"> letters</a> section, please <a href="mailto:guardian.letters@theguardian.com?body=Please%20include%20your%20name,%20full%20postal%20address%20and%20phone%20number%20with%20your%20letter%20below.%20Letters%20are%20usually%20published%20with%20the%20author%27s%20name%20and%20city/town/village.%20The%20rest%20of%20the%20information%20is%20for%20verification%20only%20and%20to%20contact%20you%20where%20necessary.">click here</a>.</strong></em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/oct/19/the-guardian-view-on-trump-and-putin-ukraines-future-is-not-theirs-to-bargain-away">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: China’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exports
item.description: <p>Third-quarter GDP up by 4.5% compared with last year as industrial output is buoyed by electronics demand</p><p>Roaring exports lifted China’s economic growth in the third quarter of this year, with factory output growing much faster than consumer spending.</p><p>China’s GDP grew by 4.5% year-on-year between July and September, the National Bureau of Statistics of China reported on Monday. The figures were better than economists had expected and up from the second quarter’s growth rate of 4.3%.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/china-economy-grows-faster-than-forecast-after-ai-boom-boosted-exports">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: The Guardian view on plague in Russia: what is most worrying is the lack of information | Editorial
item.description: <p>In the three weeks since a health worker’s death in Siberia, officials have stonewalled the WHO – setting a worrying precedent for future pandemics</p><p>Is there a plague outbreak in Russia? If the answer were a clear yes, there shouldn’t be much reason to worry. With swift medical intervention, plague is treatable. But in the nearly three weeks since <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/07/who-says-it-does-not-have-full-picture-from-russia-following-suspected-plague-death">a worker at a Siberian plague research unit</a> died of a mysterious respiratory illness, state officials have been&nbsp;consistently tight-lipped about what happened and whether there were any further cases.</p><p>It is this uncertainty that has the World Health Organization (WHO) and international community worried: partly because there is a – very small – risk of an outbreak, and partly because it is yet another warning that the international coordination we rely on&nbsp;to prevent pandemics is fraying along with the rest&nbsp;of international politics, and could easily fail to protect us in the future.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/oct/18/the-guardian-view-on-plague-in-russia-what-is-most-worrying-is-the-lack-of-information">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Why Britain should reject the lure of cheap – and scary – Chinese AI
item.description: <p>In the west the technology comes with at least some effort to provide security and a benign intent – not so from China</p><p>There is much to fear from artificial intelligence developed in China and handed to businesses and governments in the west almost free of charge.</p><p>Every month Chinese AI developers such as DeepSeek and Xiaomi dispatch the latest versions of their “open-weight” models that allow users to take the core software and use it without paying an expensive ongoing licence.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/17/why-britain-should-reject-the-lure-of-cheap-and-scary-chinese-ai">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: China’s tourists flock to experience a pretend typhoon as ‘dark tourism’ flourishes
item.description: <p>The concept of ‘paying to suffer’ soars in popularity, with simulated disasters proving a modern twist on visiting sites of historic tragedies </p><p>When Leon Lv was looking for somewhere to travel last year, she turned to the Chinese social media app RedNote for ideas. The algorithm took her to videos of people struggling to survive typhoon-strength winds and flash floods.</p><p>“I never experienced a typhoon. I don’t know how it will feel and what will happen. I just have seen it on the news,” says the 28-year-old from Chongqing in south-west China. “So that’s why I want to go there to have a safe place to experience it and learn something.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/17/china-tourists-fake-typhoon-experience-dark-tourism">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: No 10 leaves option open to impose Chinese EV tariffs if UK joins EU scheme
item.description: <p>Beijing warns against ‘discriminatory’ step after France drops opposition to British role in Made in Europe package</p><p>No 10 has left the door open to imposing tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles as part of the Made in Europe package, prompting a warning from Beijing that such a move would be “discriminatory”.</p><p>Downing Street said on Friday that it would “welcome the objective to have the UK included in the Industrial Accelerator Act” after France <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/15/france-drops-opposition-to-uk-being-included-in-made-in-europe-legislation">dropped its opposition to Britain joining the scheme</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/oct/16/uk-chinese-electric-vehicle-ev-tariffs-eu-made-in-europe-scheme">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Like dinosaur eggs in the sand: the pterosaur museum built to thrive in the Gobi desert
item.description: <p>How architects worked with harsh environment to create sustainable building in location where fossils were found</p><p>Viewed from afar, the silver-hued Hami Pterosaur Museum almost looks like a space base on Mars. Viewed from above, it resembles a collection of dinosaur eggs in the sand. Nestled in the Gobi desert, in north-west China, the new tourist attraction showcases hundreds of impressive fossils of pterosaurs, ancient flying reptiles related to dinosaurs. But far from reflecting its prehistoric exhibits, the building itself is a modern-day architectural specimen.</p><p>Designed with underground exhibition halls, giant light funnels and sprawling solar farms, the museum is able to operate sustainably while withstanding an extremely harsh environment.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/16/dinosaur-eggs-pterosaur-museum-built-gobi-desert">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, a new ‘open-weight’ AI model
item.description: <p>Meta says Muse excels at ‘multi-step reasoning’ and ‘complex software engineering’ as it races to catch up to Chinese rivals</p><p>Meta on Thursday launched a new open-weight AI model which it claims rivals, and in some cases outperforms, similar products from leading Chinese developers.</p><p>Muse Spark Open “is the most capable US open-weight model to date,” Meta’s chief of AI Alexandr Wang wrote on X.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/oct/16/meta-releases-muse-spark-open-a-new-open-weight-ai-model">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: France drops opposition to UK being included in ‘Made in Europe’ legislation
item.description: <p>British government must however align with the European Union’s position over tariffs on Chinese EVs</p><p>France has dropped its opposition to the UK being included in the EU’s “Made in Europe” legislation as long as the British government aligns with the bloc’s position over tariffs on Chinese EVs.</p><p>In a breakthrough for Andy Burnham, France on Thursday came round to backing Germany, which has always supported the UK’s calls to be designated European for the purposes of the Industrial Accelerator Act. The legislation, which is in its draft stage, is designed to protect domestic manufacturing from cheap Chinese competition.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/15/france-drops-opposition-to-uk-being-included-in-made-in-europe-legislation">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: The global economy is muddling through against the odds. But a storm is coming | Larry Elliott
item.description: <p>Finance ministers gathering for the IMF annual meeting know the need for multilateral cooperation to deal with many crises. There is little chance of that</p><p>Not much has gone right for the global economy this year, and plenty has gone wrong. Two big regional wars are destabilising prices and supply chains everywhere.<strong> </strong>Businesses and consumers are feeling the effects of a serious energy shock. Rising inflation has made it a lot more expensive for governments to finance their debts. China and the US are at loggerheads over trade.</p><p>Yet, so far, the impact has been modest. It is something of a miracle that the finance ministers and central bank governors gathered for this year’s annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in Bangkok are not having to deal with a full-blown crisis. This is not like the autumn of 2008, when the meetings took place during the worst of the global banking meltdown.</p><p>Larry Elliott is a Guardian columnist</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/oct/15/global-economy-multilateral-cooperation-crisis-imf">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: UK’s ‘incoherent’ approach to China plagued by lack of expertise, report says
item.description: <p>International alliance of China-sceptic legislators warns of risks inherent in misjudging bilateral relationship</p><p>The UK’s approach to China is “beset by incoherence” and plagued by a lack of senior expertise, according to a report warning of the risks inherent in misjudging the bilateral relationship.</p><p>An audit by the Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China (Ipac), an international grouping of China-sceptic legislators, says past engagement with Beijing has often exposed the UK to the risks of interference without delivering the opportunities promised.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/oct/14/uks-incoherent-approach-to-china-plagued-by-a-lack-of-expertise-report-says">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Excluding UK from ‘Made in Europe’ law will hurt entire EU car industry, Mercedes boss warns
item.description: <p>Ola Källenius says it will ‘weaken the industry on both sides’ ahead of act intended to counter non-EU competition </p><p>Locking the UK out of the EU’s flagship industrial “Made in Europe” legislation would amount to a “deliberate choice” by EU leaders to “hurt” the car industry across the bloc, the head of Mercedes-Benz has said.</p><p>Speaking in his capacity as president of the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association (ACEA), Ola Källenius said such a move would “weaken the industry on both sides”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/uk-made-in-europe-law-hurt-carmaking-eu-mercedes-benz-boss-ola-kallenius">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: UK resists EU pressure to hit China with tariffs
item.description: <p>Exclusive: Business secretary says he will not change trade rules due to EU pressure and denies UK will become a ‘back door’ for cheap imports</p><p>The business secretary has hit back at European demands for British tariffs on Chinese imports, saying the government will not change its trade rules because of pressure from Brussels.</p><p>Jonathan Reynolds warned that the government would not bow to calls from other countries for the UK to hit Chinese vehicles with import taxes, despite political pressure to align with the EU in exchange for deeper future economic ties.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/oct/14/uk-will-not-put-tariffs-on-chinese-vehicles-says-jonathan-reynolds">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Graduate student accused of poisoning colleague and trying to flee to China arrested at LAX
item.description: <p>Microbiologist Aili Wang, 32, poisoned tea of colleague in Wyoming who had pending patents, prosecutors allege</p><p>A Wyoming microbiology graduate student from China has been arrested on accusations she poisoned the tea of a colleague who had pending patents and with whom she did not get along, then tried to flee the country after police questioned her.</p><p>Aili Wang, 32, was arrested 6 October at Los Angeles international airport, where prosecutors allege she sought to return to China. With her were laptops, electronic storage devices and documents now in the possession of police, who allege Wang was seen on surveillance video rummaging through the desk of the victim who specialized in technology for disease treatment – research similar to work she had done in China.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/13/wyoming-student-graduate-poison-arrest">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: It’s My Time review – Michelle Yeoh excels in Rocky-style quest to be Rubik’s Cube champ
item.description: <p>True story about a former maths teacher who became a puzzle champion in retirement is squeezed into predictable sports-movie formula</p><p>It’s not quite up there with Leonardo DiCaprio <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/filmblog/2016/jan/18/fact-checking-the-revenant-leonardo-dicaprio-ray-mears">eating raw bison liver</a> to get into character, but <a href="https://www.thestar.com.my/lifestyle/entertainment/2026/07/31/michelle-yeoh-spent-two-years-mastering-the-rubik039s-cube-for-new-mandarin-film">Michelle Yeoh reportedly spent two years learning the Rubik’s Cube</a> to prepare for this Chinese drama in which she plays a real-life former maths teacher who became a champion in retirement. The true story is stretched and squeezed here, fictionalised to fit sports-movie formula; it ends up being so-so entertaining and funny in places, but disappointingly predictable. The biggest surprise is that cubing is so popular it has its own world championship.</p><p>Still, Yeoh gives a superb, spiky performance as blunt, foul-tempered Zhao Yanhong; following a stroke, Zhao is living in a nursing home where she is the resident badass, assaulting her robot care companion and making illicit trips to the off-licence. She discovers her natural talent for the Rubik’s Cube when a washed-up ex-champion called Wu Youwei (Haoran Liu) comes to the nursing home to give a tutorial. What follows is a classic sports-film structure, with qualifying heats and Zhao training day and night, lifting weights and pounding the city streets. (Yes, running is de rigueur in a Rubik’s Cube movie; physical strength is Zhao’s weak spot says Wu, who agrees to be her coach.)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/oct/13/its-my-time-review-michelle-yeoh-excels-in-rocky-style-quest-to-be-rubiks-cube-champ">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: ‘Super app’ aimed at UK students uses servers owned by Chinese firm on US blacklist
item.description: <p>ZyMix platform has contract with Tencent, which US alleges has links to People’s Liberation Army</p><p>A new messaging and payment “super app” marketed at British students uses servers owned by a Chinese company that has been put on a US military blacklist for its alleged affiliation to the People’s Liberation Army.</p><p>ZyMix, which is being pushed on university campuses as the UK’s first super app designed “for gen Z”, combining chat, payments and community features, has a contract with a German-based subsidiary of Tencent Holdings, a Chinese conglomerate in Shenzhen.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/13/super-app-uk-students-servers-china-us-blacklist">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Stellantis and Renault back UK to get EU car industry protection
item.description: <p>Bosses of Citroën owner and French carmaker also urge UK government to consider limiting imports from China</p><p>Stellantis and Renault have backed the UK car industry for inclusion in proposed rules to protect EU industry, but urged the British government to consider limiting imports of Chinese cars.</p><p>Emanuele Cappellano, who leads Stellantis’s European brands including Fiat, Citroën, Opel and Vauxhall, and François Provost, the chief executive of France’s Renault, said the UK should effectively be counted as one of the EU’s 27 member states for the purposes of the proposed <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/16/made-in-europe-laws-could-derail-uk-eu-reset-plans">“Made in Europe” legislation</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/12/stellantis-renault-uk-eu-car-industry-imports-china">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: EU to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle imports to 350,000 a year
item.description: <p>Brussels uses WTO rules to quickly impose quota, which will halve Chinese market share to 3%</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/oct/12/uk-growth-inflation-pressures-oil-price-sveriges-riksbank-nobel-prize-economic-sciences-awarded-latest-news-updates">Business live – latest updates</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/11/volkswagen-boss-backs-eu-plan-to-boost-domestic-european-industry">VW boss backs EU plan to bolster domestic industry</a></p></li></ul><p>The EU is to limit the number of hybrid electric vehicles imported from China to 350,000 cars a year, the European Commission has confirmed.</p><p>Imports have been soaring in the past two years; about 800,000 battery and plug-in hybrids are likely to be sold this year.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/12/eu-deal-china-limit-imports-hybrid-electric-vehicles">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Volkswagen boss backs EU plan to bolster domestic European industry
item.description: <p>Oliver Blume says ‘Made in Europe’ rules to counter rapid rise of lower-price Chinese brands ‘must reward real value creation’</p><p>The boss of Volkswagen has backed EU proposals to boost its domestic industry, arguing European carmakers need to be able to “compete under comparable conditions” with Chinese rivals.</p><p>Oliver Blume said “Made in Europe” rules from the EU “must reward real value creation in Europe”, speaking in Paris before the motor show this week.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/11/volkswagen-boss-backs-eu-plan-to-boost-domestic-european-industry">Continue reading...</a>
